comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Landed in c5eb21b (the view out) and ed30a27 (the four requests in).

Deviated from the plan on one point: the view carries structure and identity, not agent state. A pane's state moves far more often than the arrangement it sits in, so carrying it in the view would repaint the tree every time an agent blinked - and agent state already has exactly one writer, which is the property keeping it correct. PaneStateChanged keeps it.

Three things this turned up:

- herdr's pane.split takes target_pane_id, not pane_id, and an unknown key is ignored rather than refused. The wrong name reads as splits landing in arbitrary places. Every other pane verb takes pane_id. Caught only because the test asserts which pane ended up under which axis; counting panes was satisfied by the wrong answer.
- A tab's pane list and its tree are published separately, and splitting a two-pane tab publishes a one-pane tree in between. Composition had been reading the tree as evidence a pane was gone, which moved the keyboard and kept it moved. Fixed in c5eb21b; the herdr behavior itself still needs recording (a_27WZ30MO1).
- pane.read is a usable screen oracle with no client attached, which is what let the seam test assert 'the text landed in this pane and not that one' without a bridge.

Left for the shell card: nothing renders the view yet. Core.swift logs that it arrived and says which card renders it.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The seam pushes one pane's agent state and takes one pane's input. A
window showing a tree needs to be told the tree, and a person who wants
a split needs somewhere to ask for one.

Out: the whole region tree, absolute and idempotent, in the same
discipline the daemon's own events follow - split nodes with direction
and ratio, pane leaves carrying id, agent state and that pane's control
socket. Whole-view rather than incremental is what keeps the shell
dumb. proto/muster.proto already anticipates this in a comment on
PaneStateChanged.

In: split, close, focus and set-split-ratio. herdr answers all four
already (pane.split, pane.close, pane.focus, layout.set_split_ratio),
so what this adds is the core dispatching them - which is where "one
action path" stops being a principle and becomes the thing a CLI and an
agent-facing API will reuse verbatim.
title: 🔌 The seam grows a view, and a way to act on it
